tour.name: Antelope Canyon & Horseshoe Bend Private 2-Day Tour from Las Vegas
tour.subtitle: Two days in the slot canyons and red rock of northern Arizona with a local guide and vehicle: Zion National Park on the way, sunset at Horseshoe Bend, a Navajo-guided tour of Antelope Canyon with its shafts of light, Lake Powell and the Glen Canyon Dam.

tour.overview:
In northern Arizona, on Navajo land near the town of Page, Antelope Canyon is a slot canyon carved by flash floods into the Navajo sandstone, its smooth, flowing walls glowing orange and purple when sunlight filters in from above. Nearby, at Horseshoe Bend, the Colorado River makes a perfect loop some 300 metres below the cliff edge.

This private two-day tour takes you from Las Vegas with a local guide and a vehicle, through Zion National Park on the way, with a night in Page so you can see Horseshoe Bend at sunset and Antelope Canyon at the best time of day.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 2 days, 1 night
• Start and end: your hotel in Las Vegas
• Type: private tour with local guide, vehicle and driver; Navajo-guided canyon tour; 1 night with breakfast
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability, your hotel and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; stairs in Lower Antelope Canyon

WHAT YOU SEE
• Zion National Park.
• Horseshoe Bend.
• Upper or Lower Antelope Canyon.
• Lake Powell and the Glen Canyon Dam.

WHY THIS WORKS
Antelope Canyon is about 4 hours 30 minutes from Las Vegas; a night in Page avoids a punishing day and gives you the canyon at midday light.

WHO IT SUITS
Photographers, nature lovers, families and couples.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For a longer trip including the Grand Canyon and Monument Valley, choose our USA West 10-day tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Antelope Canyon can only be visited with an authorised Navajo guide; tours sell out and are timed. Bags are not allowed inside. Flash floods can close the canyon.

days.name: Las Vegas to Page through Zion, and sunset at Horseshoe Bend
days.description:
What to expect: the red rock country of southern Utah and sunset over the Colorado.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 7:00 and drive north-east into Utah to Zion National Park, where the Zion–Mount Carmel Highway climbs through a tunnel and past the Checkerboard Mesa, with towering sandstone cliffs. After lunch (not included) in Kanab, you continue to Page, Arizona.

In the late afternoon, you walk the short trail, about 1.2 kilometres each way, to the edge of Horseshoe Bend, where the green Colorado River curves around a sandstone spur far below, and watch the sunset.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:00 – Pick-up in Las Vegas.
10:00 – Zion National Park.
12:30 – Lunch in Kanab.
15:00 – Arrival in Page and check-in.
Sunset – Horseshoe Bend.

GOOD TO KNOW
• There is no shade on the Horseshoe Bend trail: bring water.

INCLUDED: vehicle, guide, park entrance, parking.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, dinner.

Overnight: hotel in Page.
Meals: none.

days.name: Antelope Canyon, Lake Powell and back to Las Vegas
days.description:
What to expect: the slot canyon with a Navajo guide and the drive back.

After breakfast, a Navajo guide leads you into Antelope Canyon. In Upper Antelope, you walk on the sandy floor of a narrow corridor between curving walls, and around midday, from spring to autumn, shafts of sunlight beam down to the floor. In Lower Antelope, you descend metal stairs into a deeper, narrower canyon of twisting passages. Your guide explains the Navajo name, Tsé bighánílíní, 'the place where water runs through rocks', and shows you the best angles for photos.

You then stop at the Glen Canyon Dam and an overlook above Lake Powell, a reservoir of blue water between red cliffs, before driving back to Las Vegas, arriving at about 19:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Breakfast.
09:30 – Antelope Canyon tour.
11:30 – Glen Canyon Dam and Lake Powell.
12:30 – Lunch in Page.
13:30 – Drive back to Las Vegas.
19:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Light beams in Upper Antelope are best from late March to early October around midday.
• Bring only a phone or camera; bags are not allowed.

INCLUDED: vehicle, guide, Navajo tour and permit, breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: breakfast.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability, hotels and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Which part of Antelope Canyon do we visit?
faq.answer: Upper or Lower, depending on availability and your preference. Upper is level; Lower has stairs and ladders.

faq.question: Can we enter Antelope Canyon without a guide?
faq.answer: No. It is on Navajo land and only open with authorised Navajo guides.

faq.question: What happens if the canyon closes?
faq.answer: If flash floods close it, we offer an alternative slot canyon or a refund of the tour.

faq.question: What kind of hotel is used?
faq.answer: A comfortable hotel in Page with breakfast.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Upper Antelope is flat and sandy; Lower has steep stairs. Horseshoe Bend has an accessible path.

faq.question: Can we add a boat trip on Lake Powell?
What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light layers, closed shoes, a hat and sun cream; warm clothes in winter.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: March to October for light beams; spring and autumn for comfortable temperatures.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in the United States: 15 to 20 percent is usual for guides and drivers if you were happy with the service, but it is always your choice.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
